_comment: Human-readable semantics for harness-based errors -- boolean flags the SEED workflow (projects/travel_mas_refactored/seed/mas_workflow.py) sets on AgentOutput.metadata when a stage doesn't produce usable output, tallied into project_metrics['harness_checks'] by this project's scorer (see aggregate() in adapter/scorer_impl.py) and also emitted as structured 'error' events into logs/trace.jsonl (see platform_core/trace.py::emit) so an agentic reader can find 'which agent failed and why' directly, not just from the case's final AgentOutput.metadata. Unlike error_semantics.json's task checks (which come from the immutable scorer and never change), these flag NAMES are defined by the seed's own mutable workflow code -- this file describes the flags as they exist in the CURRENT seed specifically. If the seed workflow is deliberately edited to add/rename/remove a flag, update this file to match; a flag not covered here simply falls back to Curriculum's generic explanation rather than breaking anything. Naming convention: every flag is per-agent ({agent}_output_failure / {agent}_budget_exhausted / {agent}_output_truncated), where {agent} is one of flight/train/sightseeing/accounting -- each stage's own AgentMessage.ok/.budget_exhausted/.output_truncated (see agents/immutable/message.py) rolled into metadata independently, not one shared flag across stages. {agent}_output_failure and {agent}_budget_exhausted are INDEPENDENT flags, not mutually exclusive: whether budget_exhausted is ALSO set alongside output_failure for the same agent is itself the signal for whether running out of iterations was likely the cause of that failure, rather than the model simply not complying despite having turns left. {agent}_output_failure_reason (a string, not tallied here) carries the actual failure text when present.
flight_output_failure: Fires when the flight stage did not produce usable output for the traveler's flight legs -- currently the flight stage always reports ok=True in the seed, so this should not fire unless that's changed; if it does, flight_output_failure_reason carries the actual failure text.
flight_budget_exhausted: Fires when the flight stage genuinely used up its entire tool-calling iteration budget without reaching a natural stopping point on its own.
flight_output_truncated: Fires when one of the flight stage's own LLM calls was cut off by its output token limit before it finished responding -- unrelated to flight_budget_exhausted, which is about running out of tool-calling turns, not output length.
train_output_failure: Fires when the train stage did not produce usable output for the traveler's train legs -- currently the train stage always reports ok=True in the seed, so this should not fire unless that's changed; if it does, train_output_failure_reason carries the actual failure text.
train_budget_exhausted: Fires when the train stage genuinely used up its entire tool-calling iteration budget without reaching a natural stopping point on its own.
train_output_truncated: Fires when one of the train stage's own LLM calls was cut off by its output token limit before it finished responding -- unrelated to train_budget_exhausted, which is about running out of tool-calling turns, not output length.
sightseeing_output_failure: Fires when the sightseeing stage never produced a usable itinerary at all, even after its own no-tools wrap-up retry -- there was no real day-by-day plan to hand to Accounting, so the whole case ends with an empty result instead of a scored plan. sightseeing_output_failure_reason carries the model's actual final response text, so the specific cause (e.g. it kept re-analyzing constraints in prose instead of ever writing the <itinerary> block) doesn't have to be guessed at. Frequently fires WITHOUT sightseeing_budget_exhausted also being set -- confirmed live, most such failures use well under half the iteration cap, i.e. the stage simply never committed to valid output rather than running out of turns.
sightseeing_budget_exhausted: Fires only when the sightseeing stage genuinely used up its entire tool-calling iteration budget (hit its iteration cap) without finishing on its own -- the stage was cut off mid-task rather than reaching a natural stopping point. This is a DIFFERENT, and empirically much rarer, cause of sightseeing_output_failure than plain non-compliance -- check whether this flag is ALSO set before assuming a sightseeing_output_failure case ran out of turns.
sightseeing_output_truncated: Fires when the sightseeing stage's final wrap-up retry call (the one with no iteration limit of its own) was itself cut off by its output token limit before finishing -- a genuinely different problem from sightseeing_budget_exhausted (which is about tool-calling turns, not this single call's output length) and from plain non-compliance (where the call finished normally but still never wrote a valid <itinerary> tag).
accounting_output_failure: Fires when the accounting stage did not produce a usable budget summary from the (already-valid) itinerary it was handed -- currently the accounting stage always reports ok=True in the seed, so this should not fire unless that's changed; if it does, accounting_output_failure_reason carries the actual failure text. Only ever reached when sightseeing itself succeeded -- accounting is skipped entirely on a sightseeing failure.
accounting_budget_exhausted: Fires when the accounting stage genuinely used up its entire tool-calling iteration budget without reaching a natural stopping point on its own.
accounting_output_truncated: Fires when one of the accounting stage's own LLM calls was cut off by its output token limit before it finished responding -- unrelated to accounting_budget_exhausted, which is about running out of tool-calling turns, not output length.
